artist_profile: Per Brian's call, processed as R&B (no artist dig). Nasty Nati is an R&B/funk BRASS band — sousaphone, trombone, tenor & alto sax, trumpet fronting the rhythm section, so the horn section is the identity and gets slotted as a section (each horn owns a frequency lane).
research_summary: Genre fixed R&B by Brian (no artist research). Per-source fresh web pass (Shure/Audix/Audio-Technica/Sennheiser specs + Gearspace/PSW + masteringthemix/musicguymixing R&B-drum consensus) cross-checked vs KB mic-library + eq-starting-points, and beside Brian's console-verified Izzy Escobar 2.0 build (same FSQ house kit). Backline (Backstage Backline pull 26-0420): Mapex Saturn V kit (22" kick, 10/12/16 toms, 14" Black Panther snare), Sabian HHX cymbals, Yamaha CP33 keys. Weather (Open-Meteo, 6–10pm): 7/25 77–83°F, 43–61% RH, wind 4–8 mph, rain ~1% — HF carries a touch better; don't over-boost the top.
room_context: Open-air Fountain Square — no room gain, low end + HF dissipate over the throw, façade slap but no reverb tail. Cuts run deeper than indoor (−6 to −9 typ), HPF decisive, clarity first. L-Acoustics A15/KS21 house PA, M32 monitors.
changes: Kick-out D6 (vs Izzy's 52A): near-flat — NO 3–5k boost (capsule bakes +5k) and NO 600 cut (already −15 scooped).
Added snare-bottom e604: HPF 180, owns wire snap only; i5 keeps body/crack.
OH is a Beta 27 STEREO pair on fader 9 (not SM81 split 9/10) — top already baked, so no HF boost, tame 9k; ch 10 stays the PL8 return.
Bass two-mic INVERTED vs Izzy: PG52 (kick mic on the cab) owns sub/thump, DI owns definition — de-stacked the DI lows.
Four guitars: e609 (1/2) voiced against SM57 (3/4) so the mids don't pile.
Vocals override the FSQ template's wireless curve/feedback notch — ring out at soundcheck.
decisions: Q: Percussion 1/2 instrument? -> Brian: generic aux perc — conservative, neutral voicing.
Genre fixed R&B for all three by Brian; no artist research.

reverbs.plugin_eq: LC 180 Hz on the return; ducker Reverb mode, Thr −22 dB
reverbs.why: Lead-vocal sheen + presence, sits forward over the band; no room outdoors to muddy it — the workhorse lead plate.

reverbs.why: Gives place without wash on up-tempo/funk material; hands off to the Vocal Plate when a song slows down.

reverbs.settings: Decay 0.6s (factory) · PreDelay 0 · VLF −12 (cut hard from 0 factory — always cut) · E/L Max Early · Late −10 · Late Rolloff 6800 (factory)

reverb_pairing: Vocal Plate is the default lead — forward and present. On up-tempo/funk numbers switch the lead to the tighter Vocal Chamber so the groove stays dry and articulate; the two hand off song-to-song. Gold Hall is the big-moment throw only — a feature or a ballad — never under the whole set. Brass Hall sits under the horn section as its own return so the five clip mics glue into one section; keep it below the vocal returns so it doesn't stack mud. Snare Plate A feeds the reserved ch-10 PL8 return for backbeat depth; Studio B Close is a whisper of kit glue only. Everything runs 100% wet on its own return, VLF cut, Late higher than a Memo send because there's no room to carry the tail.

channels.name: Kick In
channels.notes: Beta 91A/D6 kick blend — 91A is the attack/click layer. Treat the pair as ONE: same VCA, pan together, blend constant. Polarity: sum in mono, flip one if thinner. Bus: notch −2/−3 @300–500 if it builds.
channels.mic_notes: Beta 91A boundary inside the kick — the click/attack engine. Contour assumed FLAT (the 400 cut lives on the desk; if the switch is engaged, halve it). Owns click + upper; lows tucked under the D6.
channels.eq_summary: +4@3k beater definition that travels outdoors (R&B punch, not a metal click). 400/250 clear the shell boom the boundary picks up — eased for open air. Lows modest (+2@80) so they don't stack with the D6's baked 63Hz. TRACE: base(91A boundary, +4@3k click) · equip(22" Mapex Saturn kick — no change) · genre(R&B — punch over click) · artist(no dig) · venue(FSQ — box cuts eased, no room mud). COMP (doc only, not patched): Green FET ~4:1, 15ms atk, 3–4 dB GR.

channels.name: Kick Out
channels.notes: Beta 91A/D6 kick blend — D6 is the sub/body core. Pan together, same VCA.
channels.mic_notes: Audix D6 pre-scooped 'smiley' — peaks ~63Hz & ~5kHz, deep scoop −15dB @600. Thump+click baked in; needs almost no EQ. Owns the sub/body under the 91A's click.
channels.eq_summary: Barely touched — the capsule IS the kick voicing. +3@60 supports the low open air swallows; light 250 trim. Capsule-voicing gate: NO 3–5k boost (D6 already bakes +5k — a boost stacks harsh) and NO 600 cut (already −15 scooped). TRACE: base(D6 smiley — near-flat) · equip(22" kick — no change) · genre(R&B thump) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ — +60 for lost low). Two-mic: D6 owns sub, 91A owns click.

channels.name: Snare Top
channels.notes: Snare top/bottom pair — treat with the e604 as one snare; polarity-check the pair.
channels.mic_notes: i5 bakes +5dB@150 body + a strong +9dB@5.5k presence, mids slightly scooped — more open/body than a 57. Owns the snare body + crack; the e604 owns the wire snap.
channels.eq_summary: Capsule-voicing gate: the +9@5.5k is baked, so I TRIM it −2 (not boost) and put the snap up at 7k where the capsule rolls off. +3@1k crack, −5@300 box (eased — the i5 isn't boxy, don't gut it). TRACE: base(i5 +9@5.5k baked → trim) · equip(14" Black Panther — no change) · genre(R&B backbeat — body over crack) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ — 7k snap to cut outdoors). GATE (doc): fast ~1ms atk but ghost notes/press rolls must live — 15–20ms rel. Two-mic: i5 body+crack, e604 snap.

channels.name: Snare Bot
channels.notes: Bottom head — wire capture only. Polarity-check against the snare top; flip if the pair thins.
channels.mic_notes: e604 clip on the bottom head — scooped low-mids, voiced attack, thin lows (ideal for wires). Owns the snare-wire snap/sizzle only.
channels.eq_summary: HPF way up at 180 so it's wires, not shell or kick bleed. +3@8k snap; −3@1k clears the e604's box. Lane: owns the top-end wire sizzle, the i5 owns body — no overlap. TRACE: base(e604 thin/voiced-attack) · equip(snare wires) · genre(R&B — crisp backbeat) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ — 8k to cut). GATE (doc): key off the snare top so wires don't chatter.

channels.name: Hat
channels.mic_notes: SM81 — ruler-flat, un-hyped highs. Takes EQ straight; no built-in flattery to fight.
channels.eq_summary: No HF boost (81 is already detailed and dry 7/24 air thins the top over the throw anyway — don't make it brittle). Clear the low bleed (800) + the 2k clang so it sparkles clean. TRACE: base(SM81 flat) · equip(14" HHX hats) · genre(R&B — tight hat) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ+dry — resist top boost).

channels.name: Rack 1
channels.mic_notes: D2 tuned to control tom resonance — articulate with little EQ; leaner deep lows than the D4.
channels.eq_summary: Attack lift +4@2.8k (trust the capsule), gentle 135 body, modest 450 mud cut. TRACE: base(D2 — articulate) · equip(10" Saturn rack) · genre(R&B fills) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ). GATE (doc): snappy release for funk; don't choke the decay.

channels.name: Rack 2
channels.mic_notes: As Rack 1, shifted down for the larger 12" drum.
channels.eq_summary: Let the D2 do the work; body at 120 for the bigger shell. TRACE: base(D2) · equip(12" Saturn rack) · genre · artist(—) · venue(FSQ).

channels.name: Floor
channels.mic_notes: D4 reaches ~an octave lower than the D2 natively; smooth 800–1k (not scooped) — may want a touch of click.
channels.eq_summary: Body shelf modest +4@70 (support, not a lift; ride the sub outdoors). +4@1.8k stick definition the D4 lacks. TRACE: base(D4 — deep, smooth mids) · equip(16" Saturn floor) · genre(R&B) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ — modest sub). GATE (doc): slower release than the racks so the floor decay lives.

channels.name: OH (st)
channels.notes: STEREO pair on fader 9 (both OH mics on this one fader). FSQ ch 10 is the SNARE PL8 return — not an input.
channels.mic_notes: Beta 27 LDC pair as overheads — flat 60Hz–3k with baked +2dB bumps at 5.5k & 9k, supercardioid (tight, less room — good outdoors), −15 pad available.
channels.eq_summary: Capsule-voicing gate: the top is already lifted (5.5k+9k baked) → NO HF boost; a light −2@9k tames fizz instead. −5@300 clears low wash + kit bleed so it's cymbals/sheen, not a room mic. Supercardioid keeps the outdoor stage tight. HPF 200. TRACE: base(Beta 27 — baked top) · equip(HHX cymbals) · genre(R&B — cymbal sheen) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ — supercard tight, clear wash).

channels.name: Bass DI
channels.notes: Bass DI + PG52 cab blend — INVERTED lanes: DI = definition/mids/top, PG52 = sub/thump. Group to one VCA, polarity-check against the PG52.
channels.mic_notes: Bass DI — clean, full-range. The PG52 (a kick mic) is on the cab. LANE: the DI owns note definition + mids + upper harmonics; the PG52 owns the sub/thump — so the DI's lows are pulled back to de-stack.
channels.eq_summary: R&B/soul bass = round, low-mid forward, top rolled. +4@700 note/growl (DI's lane), −4@1.5k tames string clank, −5@250 de-stacks off the PG52's low body, +3@80 modest (PG52 carries the real sub). TRACE: base(DI clean — definition lane) · equip(bass rig, DI+cab) · genre(R&B — round, low-mid forward) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ — support 80). COMP (doc): opto ~3:1, 20–30ms atk, even the pocket.

channels.name: Bass Mic
channels.notes: Blend with the DI — see Bass DI note. PG52 carries the lows.
channels.mic_notes: PG52 is a kick mic on the bass cab — 30Hz–13k, tuned low-end thump + a slight upper-mid click bump, rolls off above 13k (no air). It's the SUB/BODY layer under the DI.
channels.eq_summary: Owns the low thump: +4@90 shelf. −5@400 carves a pocket so it doesn't double the DI's mud. Small +2@2.5k for finger attack (the PG52's click bump). LPF 8k — no useful top, keep it dark body. TRACE: base(PG52 kick-mic-on-cab — sub lane) · equip(bass cab) · genre(R&B thump) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ). Two-mic: PG52 lows, DI definition — no low boost on both.

channels.name: Gtr 1
channels.notes: Four guitars (1/2 = e609, 3/4 = SM57) — pan-spread, freq-staggered so the mids don't pile.
channels.mic_notes: e609 flat-face over the cab — bright upper-mid/presence 4–5k, supercardioid, can get edgy 2.5–4k on bright amps. Owns cab presence.
channels.eq_summary: Rhythm R&B guitar sits under the vocal + horns. −3@3k tames the e609 edge; +2@1.2k so the comp speaks; −4@400 box; HPF 100 + −3@150 keeps it out of the bass. TRACE: base(e609 — bright/edgy) · equip(gtr cab) · genre(R&B comp — supportive, not a wall) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ — deeper box cut). Staggered vs the 57 guitars.

channels.name: Gtr 2
channels.notes: See Gtr 1 — shifted for separation from Gtr 1.
channels.mic_notes: e609 as Gtr 1; voiced a hair different (edge 2.8k, presence 1.4k) so two e609 guitars don't overlay.
channels.eq_summary: As Gtr 1 with the edge/presence shifted so the two e609 guitars separate. TRACE: base(e609) · equip(gtr cab) · genre(R&B comp) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ).

channels.name: Gtr 3
channels.notes: SM57 guitars (3/4) voiced with presence UP where the e609 guitars are cut — that's the 4-guitar separation.
channels.mic_notes: SM57 on the cab — mid-forward, presence 3–5k, builds box/honk 300–500. Owns mid grit.
channels.eq_summary: +3@3.5k presence (57's lane — differs from the e609 guitars' voicing so 4 gtrs separate), −5@400 box, −2@800 honk, HPF 100 + 180 trim off the bass. TRACE: base(SM57 — mid grit) · equip(gtr cab) · genre(R&B — present, under the vocals) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ — deeper box).

channels.name: Gtr 4
channels.mic_notes: SM57 as Gtr 3; presence at 3k, box 450 so the two 57 guitars separate.
channels.eq_summary: As Gtr 3, shifted. TRACE: base(SM57) · equip(gtr cab) · genre(R&B) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ).

channels.name: Sousa
channels.mic_notes: AT Pro 35 clip on the sousaphone bell — 50Hz–15k, 80Hz rolloff 18dB/oct, strong lows (good for low brass), rounded top, 145 SPL. The LOW-brass foundation.
channels.eq_summary: Sousaphone is the bass of the brass band — +3@90 weight, +2@1.2k so the line has pitch definition (not just thump), −4@350 mud in the dense horn stack. LPF 8k (no useful top). Owns the sub-brass lane; sits below the bass guitar's 80. TRACE: base(Pro 35 — strong lows) · equip(sousaphone) · genre(funk brass — walking foundation) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ). COMP (doc): opto ~3:1, 20ms, even the line.

channels.name: Bone
channels.mic_notes: Pro 35 clip on the bell — rounded top means gentle presence. Trombone owns the low-brass midrange ~1k.
channels.eq_summary: Section slotting: the bone owns ~1k, so its bark cut sits there (−3@1.2k) — trumpet's cut goes higher, sax lower. −4@500 mud, +2@6k rasp for definition over the Pro 35's rolled top. TRACE: base(Pro 35 rounded top) · equip(trombone) · genre(funk brass — fast transients) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ). COMP (doc): fast atk ~5ms — brass transients jump.

channels.name: Tenor
channels.mic_notes: Pro 35 clip at the bell — tenor sax, lower reed. Upper-mid harshness + body resonance; needs upper harmonics to cut a dense mix.
channels.eq_summary: Section slotting: tenor's honk cut at 800 (lowest reed), below the alto (1.5k) and trumpet (2.7k) so the horns don't pile. −4@350 body, +3@7k reed air to cut over the rolled top. TRACE: base(Pro 35) · equip(tenor sax) · genre(funk horns) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ). Watch the plasticky upper-mid up close.

channels.name: Alto
channels.mic_notes: Pro 35 clip — alto sax, brighter reed than the tenor. Owns ~1.5k in the section.
channels.eq_summary: Alto honk cut at 1.5k (its lane, above the tenor's 800), −3@400 body, +3@8k air. Slots between tenor and trumpet. TRACE: base(Pro 35) · equip(alto sax) · genre(funk horns) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ).

channels.name: Tpt
channels.mic_notes: Pro 35 clip on the bell — trumpet, the brightest/loudest horn, transients jump. Owns the top of the section ~2.7k.
channels.eq_summary: Trumpet's bark cut sits highest in the section (−4@2.7k) — tenor@800, bone@1.2k, alto@1.5k, trumpet@2.7k, so each horn owns a lane and they don't pile. −3@500 body, +2@9k sizzle. TRACE: base(Pro 35 rounded top) · equip(trumpet) · genre(funk horns — lead bark) · artist(—) · venue(FSQ). COMP (doc): fast atk mandatory — trumpet spikes above the mix.

channels.name: Wls 1
channels.mic_notes: Beta 58A supercardioid handheld — TWO baked presence peaks (~4k & ~10k), boxy ~600, <500 attenuated, tight pattern/high GBF (brighter than an SM58). LEAD voicing.
channels.eq_summary: Cut-only (feedback + taste). Dynamic de-ess −3@10k on the baked top peak so the air stays between sibilants; light −2@4k tames stridency without killing the bite the capsule bakes; −4@600 box for outdoor intelligibility. HPF 100. Overrides the FSQ template wireless curve/notch — ring out at soundcheck; reach for comp + a touch of plate before more EQ. TRACE: base(Beta 58A twin peaks) · genre(R&B lead) · venue(FSQ intelligibility).
